title: Aftermath of Heavenly Tribulation
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was staring at the Tianji Diagram in a daze, an old yet familiar voice suddenly rang out from the void: 'You finally found this place, successor... This is the last letter the First Observer left for you.' Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul slowly formed, holding a yellowed ancient slip in his hand, the Dao patterns flowing on it were exactly the same as those on the Tianji Record Fragment.

text.content: Dawn in the Imperial Capital came especially slowly, as if even the Heavenly Dao was mourning for the catastrophe of last night. Chen Ji stood on the ruins of the imperial city, the morning wind blowing past, his thin figure swaying slightly, yet he managed to steady himself. The price of ten years of lifespan was heavier than he had anticipated—the few strands of stark silver at his temples were the most merciless brand of time. In the distance came the cries of the common people and calls for rescue from beneath the ruins, each sound entering his ears, yet he could only clench his fists until his knuckles turned white. 'Transmit my command,' his voice was hoarse but resolute, 'Tianqing Sect disciples shall immediately engage in rescue efforts. Regardless of faction or sect, anyone willing to lend aid may come to the Imperial City's Council Hall to receive rewards.'

Su Qingyao stepped forward urgently, supporting Chen Ji's swaying body with one arm. The moment her hand touched his arm, her heart shuddered—he whose muscles were once as steady as bedrock were now so thin they were just skin and bone, cold to the touch. She suddenly remembered last night's shocking scene: the Tianji Record shining brilliantly, Chen Ji surrounded by flowing Dao rhyme like a river, yet his face had aged ten years in that instant. 'Heavenly Fate Value... how much did you consume?' Her voice trembled, eyes reddening, yet she bit her lip hard to keep from losing composure. This usually cold and proud Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, at this moment had only heartache and self-blame in her eyes—she knew each time he used the Tianji Record came at a price, yet she could only watch as he burned his life force to protect this city.

Chen Ji gently pushed away Su Qingyao's hand, a faint smile curling at the corner of his mouth. That smile, in her eyes, wounded her more than any injury could. He turned to gaze at the devastated Imperial Capital, his voice low but clear: 'There are hundreds of thousands of common people in this city. If I hadn't acted, the aftermath of Heavenly Tribulation would have turned everything to dust. Ten years of life for hundreds of thousands of lives...' He paused, his gaze deep as an abyss, 'If Father were still alive, he would have made the same choice.' Before the words even finished, a violent coughing fit struck. He covered his mouth with his sleeve, yet could not hide the spots of blood seeping between his fingers.

Su Qingyao dragged Chen Ji's arm without question, forcefully pulling him deeper into the imperial city. Her steps were urgent yet determined, each one carrying unwavering obstinacy: 'Last night I detected residual formation fluctuations under the western ruins... that aura, it was identical to the Tianji Record.' Upon hearing this, Chen Ji's exhausted eyes suddenly flashed with brilliance. He understood his father Chen Xuan's legacy better than anyone—that man seemed dissolute and carefree on the surface, but was actually meticulous in his thoughts, surely leaving contingencies before his death. The two of them passed through layers upon layers of rubble, stopping before a half-collapsed side hall. Su Qingyao raised her jade-like hand, a clear radiance sweeping across the debris—however, the ground slowly cracked open, revealing a blue stone staircase extending downward, and on the walls on both sides were clearly inscribed Dao patterns identical to those on the Tianji Record Fragment!

dialogue.content: Father... he foresaw this day long ago.

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at those Dao patterns, a surge of indescribable sorrow rising in his heart. From childhood he had been treated as waste, bullied by fellow disciples, while Father never stood up for him, instead drinking and carousing every day, living without restraint. He had resented, despaired, lost all hope... until now, he finally understood the profound meaning hidden behind that man's silence: not refusing to protect, but wanting him to forge a truly resilient spirit through adversity; not neglecting to manage, but using this method to gradually pass on the truth of the Tianji Record to him. 'Lead the way.' He took a deep breath, suppressed his churning emotions, and descended step by step into the golden-light-filled secret chamber.

The chamber was not large, yet was arranged with exquisite precision. Nine maps of Heavenly Dao evolution hung on the four walls, and at the center stood an ancient stone table, on which lay a completely golden silk scroll—the very Tianji Diagram in its entirety! Chen Ji stepped forward slowly, his hands trembling as he unfolded the silk scroll. In an instant, countless Dao patterns rose from the diagram, transforming into a curtain of light that enveloped him entirely. What appeared in the light curtain were not words, but scenes: a solitary figure standing at the edge of the Void, behind him the remnants of countless stars, and right before that figure, a rift as black as ink was slowly tearing apart...

The scene in the light curtain shifted abruptly. That figure—a being wearing plain white robes with an indistinct face—was gazing at the black rift, seemingly contemplating, seemingly deciding. After a long while, he extended his hand and inscribed a mark in the Void. That mark transformed into flowing light, entering the myriad worlds of existence, then vanished without a trace. And in the instant the mark disappeared, the rift suddenly expanded, countless distorted tentacles emerging from within, sweeping toward that white-robed figure... The scene cut off abruptly. 'He left.' Chen Ji murmured to himself, his voice carrying a tremor, 'The First Observer discovered the source of the invasion, yet chose to depart proactively... He was leading those things away!'

choice.prompt: The secrets of the Tianji Diagram are shocking, but the reconstruction of the Imperial Capital is equally urgent. Chen Ji must make a choice—continue investigating the truth, or stabilize the overall situation first.

choices.description: The common people of the Imperial Capital are suffering in dire straits. Investigating now would only cause more people to lose hope. Save lives first, then trace the roots.
choices.visible_cost: The truth may become harder to trace as time passes
choices.visible_reward: Popular support is gained, reputation soars
choices.risk_hint: May miss the best timing to investigate the truth

dialogue.content: I knew you would choose this.

text.content: Su Qingyao gazed at Chen Ji's pale profile, a soft light flickering in her eyes. She drew an elixir from her sleeve and, without asking, pressed it into his palm: 'Take this first. You looking like this when meeting those disaster victims will only make the situation worse.' The elixir dissolved the moment it entered his mouth, a warmth flowing through his meridians. Chen Ji felt his depleted essence, energy, and spirit recover somewhat. He looked at her, lips parting, yet finally only uttered: 'Thank you.' The two walked out of the secret chamber together, beginning the long and arduous path of reconstruction.

result_nodes.description: If the source of the dimensional invasion is not uncovered, today's catastrophe will surely recur. Better to strike proactively than to wait for the next blow.

result_nodes.risk_hint: If the investigation stalls, the Imperial Capital may face upheaval again

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at the Tianji Diagram once more, carving every Dao pattern trajectory into his mind. The light curtain appeared again, and this time he saw more: after the First Observer departed, the black rift did not heal, but continued eroding the boundaries of the myriad worlds over the long ages. Every 'Heavenly Dao Cycle' was a reinforcement of the seal... and also an expansion of the rift. He suddenly realized that what they called the Heavenly Will and the cycles of fate were merely an endless war—and that all of them were merely pieces on a board. 'Interesting.' He laughed softly, yet the smile was full of bitterness, 'So after all this struggle, we have been on that person's chessboard.'

Just then, a faint glow suddenly emerged from the depths of the secret chamber. Chen Ji followed the light and saw that beneath the stone table was embedded a dark golden token, its patterns resonating with those on the Tianji Diagram one by one. He bent down to retrieve the token, and the instant his palm touched the cold metal, a familiar aura entered his consciousness—it was Father's aura! On the back of the token were inscribed a few small characters. Chen Ji examined them for a long while before his pupils contracted sharply: 'My son, if you have reached this point, it means the Tianji Record has accepted you as its master. The truth lies beneath your feet... Go to the First Observer's Dao Temple and find his final legacy. But be careful, there are guardians there—' The text ended abruptly, as if the writer had been forced to stop by some intervention.

Chen Ji slowly shook his head, his gaze profound: 'What Father means is... after the First Observer left, his Dao Temple did not vanish, but was sealed somewhere.' He tucked the token into his sleeve, turning to face the chamber exit, 'According to the Tianji Diagram, the source of dimensional invasion comes from the Void rift, and the First Observer's Dao Temple... perhaps lies at the deepest part of that rift.' He suddenly recalled something, his expression shifting: 'There is one more thing—the Tianji Diagram mentions that the 'Key of Heavenly Fate' is the only key to open the Dao Temple.' His voice trembled slightly, that name lodged in his throat, a name he had not spoken in years: Nian'er.

Chen Ji did not answer, only gazing at the sky beyond the secret chamber, a rare softness and guilt flickering in his eyes. He remembered that rainy night, his young sister forcibly taken away, he chased desperately yet could do nothing. At that time he was too weak, too weak to even protect his own family. 'Twelve years.' His voice was very soft, as if speaking only to himself, 'Holy Sect... what you owe me, it's time to repay.' Su Qingyao stood quietly to the side, gazing at his desolate silhouette, an indescribable emotion rising in her heart. This man never showed weakness before others, yet at this moment, she clearly felt that deep, grievous wound in his heart.

choice.prompt: The clues Father left point to the First Observer's Dao Temple, and sister Chen Nian is the 'Key of Heavenly Fate' to open it. Chen Ji must decide his next course of action.

choices.description: Chen Nian was taken by the Holy Sect twelve years ago. She is the key to opening the Dao Temple, and also the deepest concern in his heart.
choices.visible_cost: Reconstruction work may be delayed as a result
choices.visible_reward: May reunite with sister and restore the family
choices.risk_hint: Holy Sect forces run deep and complex; rash action carries enormous risk

text.content: Su Qingyao looked at his profile gazing into the distance and suddenly spoke: 'Regarding the Holy Sect matter... I can help gather information.' Her voice was as cold as ever, yet the implication within was perfectly clear to Chen Ji. She was declaring her willingness to risk danger for him. Chen Ji turned to look at her, silently for a moment, then suddenly reached out and gently patted her shoulder: 'Thank you. But this time, I cannot let you take risks for me again.' His voice was soft, yet carried undeniable resolve. Su Qingyao was stunned, then she saw the resolve deep within his eyes—this man had long since prepared to enter the tiger's den alone.

result_nodes.description: The Imperial Capital just endured a great disaster. If we leave now, it may trigger greater upheaval. Sister's matter needs to be planned carefully.
result_nodes.visible_cost: Sister may continue suffering in the Holy Sect
result_nodes.visible_reward: With more resources at command, the rescue operation will have better odds

dialogue.content: You are more of a... Sect Master than I imagined.

text.content: Su Qingyao said softly, her tone carrying a hint of complexity. Upon hearing this, Chen Ji forced a bitter smile: 'Sect Master? I cannot even protect my own sister. What kind of Sect Master am I.' He turned to gaze at the ruins beyond the secret chamber, his gaze gradually becoming resolute, 'But you are right. I cannot act on impulse. Imperial Capital stable, then the world is stable; world stable, then I will have sufficient leverage to negotiate with the Holy Sect.' He took a deep breath, deeply pressing his longing and guilt for his sister into the depths of his heart, 'Give me three months. In three months, I will bring her back with my own hands.'

dialogue.content: If you continue like this, your body will collapse.

text.content: Chen Ji smiled faintly. That smile, in Su Qingyao's eyes, made her heart tighten. This man was always like this, swallowing all hardships into his own belly, bearing all pressure alone. 'Rest assured, I know my limits.' Chen Ji said, drawing the Tianji Record Fragment from his sleeve, 'For the plan ahead, I need to use it to deduce some things.' Su Qingyao wanted to speak yet held back, ultimately just sighing and stepping aside quietly. She knew his decisions were never something she could change. And all she could do was silently guard him from behind.

Just as Chen Ji prepared to activate the Tianji Record for divination, an eerie fluctuation suddenly rippled through the secret chamber. The void's atmosphere twisted, and an old yet familiar voice rang out凭空: 'Successor, you have finally found this place.' Chen Ji's pupils contracted, the Dao technique in his hand suddenly condensing—the visitor was none other than Mo Xiansheng! That guardian existing in remnant soul form on the first page of the Tianji Record had now manifested on his own, his ethereal soul flickering in and out of visibility within the secret chamber. Su Qingyao instinctively moved to shield Chen Ji, but was gently pulled back behind him. 'Mo Xiansheng,' Chen Ji's voice was calm, 'you came faster than I anticipated.' Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul bowed slightly, those虚幻眼眸 flickering with complex light: 'This is the last letter the First Observer left... He said it may only be opened when the successor has found the Tianji Diagram.' As he spoke, an ethereal hand slowly extended, palm cradling a yellowed ancient scroll.

dialogue.content: This letter... who did he leave it for?

text.content: Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment, his soul body trembling slightly, as if reminiscing about something from distant ages: 'Before the First Observer ascended, he left a remnant consciousness across the myriad worlds. He said the successor of the Tianji Record would not be limited to just one generation, and each generation of successor would face the same choice—to become a piece, or to become the Chess Player.' His voice gradually lowered, 'This letter is his final testament to all successors. As for the contents...' He paused, those ethereal eyes staring directly at Chen Ji, 'Only you have the authority to open it.' The secret chamber fell into complete silence, only the Dao patterns flowing on that ancient scroll flickering gently, as if recounting a secret spanning countless ages.
